target: For arbitrary n>=1, determine indexed two-step Ore structure of word-quadratic AS-regular Z-domains with primitive jumps (1^n,2,3). The main all-n reduction now proves B-ASn if and only if every r3(i)=n,r5(i)=1; those two rank conditions imply the full indexed two-step Ore structure without H, Koszulity, noetherianity or initial B-AS. Thus only their automaticity remains for unconditional indexed exhaustion. This automaticity is proved for n=1,2,3; n2,n3 also descend to ordinary Ore. At n4, D=L-N=3 is unconditional and ten conditions are equivalent, including Koszulity, N6, A/B period one, uniform/standard B Hilbert rows, B-AS4, indexed/ordinary Ore, and r3=4,r5=1. Their automaticity remains open. Ordinary graded word-Koszul objects admit full two-step Ore without initial H or noetherianity. Standard bigraded row Hilbert series imply the indexed structure and Koszulity for every n. A formal n4 pure-Euler model passes all-degree positivity/growth/Hopf constraints; it is not a realized algebra. Unconditional indexed exhaustion remains open for n>=4. Additionally, r5 is forced everywhere when the AS period L is not divisible by three, and on at least one mod-three class otherwise.

scope.broad_target: Secondary n=2 target Q: primitive jumps (1,1,2,3), word-quadratic, two-sided AS4 and polynomial row/column growth over the standing algebraically closed characteristic-zero field. Word-Koszulity, AS translation +7, seven-periodicity and the standard relation counts and Hilbert series are proved, not assumed. Domain, noetherianity and period one are not imposed on this secondary all-Q target.
scope.standard_exhaustiveness: Q=H=S. The outer relation counts r_2=r_5=1 have a non-computational proof. The mixed counts r_3=r_4=2 follow from analytically derived necessary conditions and an exact finite integer elimination of the remaining rank arrays. This is a computer-assisted proof under the AS hypotheses, not certification of AS-regularity from low-degree Hilbert agreement. Automatic domainness and period one remain open.
scope.graded_ore_locus: Over C: connected locally finite left/right noetherian AS4 graded algebras with minimal generator degrees (1,1,2,3) and H(t)=1/((1-t)^2(1-t^2)(1-t^3)), classified up to graded isomorphism; relations need not be word-quadratic
scope.quadratic_graded_ore_locus: The word-quadratic part of the preceding graded locus admits a complete Ore chart allowing non-diagonal automorphisms. Its associated Z-algebras lie in H and are 1-periodic; bare indexed isomorphism is a coarser relation.
scope.general_weights: For n>=1: connected locally finite left/right noetherian AS-regular graded C-algebras with minimal generator degrees (1^n,2,3), global dimension n+2, and H(t)=1/((1-t)^n(1-t^2)(1-t^3)).
scope.general_weights_quadratic: Within the stated general-n noetherian graded Hilbert class, word-quadratic algebras are word-Koszul with relation counts (binom(n,2),n,n,1); domain objects admit the exhaustive canonical two-step Ore classification and explicit graded-isomorphism orbits. These are the hypotheses of that graded theorem, not additional assumptions authorized for the arbitrary-n indexed target. Indexed Ore exhaustion is now established independently for n=1,2,3. Universal indexed descent to one graded algebra is false by GEN-INDEXED-PERIOD-TWO, a special case of the n=1 classification; n=2,3 retain their stronger domain descent theorems. General non-word-quadratic graded exhaustion is not proved for n>=3.
scope.indexed_domain_locus: All Z-domains in Q have standard relation counts and Hilbert series, admit a word-preserving period-one structure, and are associated Z-algebras of B[z;sigma][w;tau,D] over quantum or Jordan planes. Hilbert series, noetherianity and period one are conclusions. A finite matrix criterion now decides existence of bare indexed isomorphisms; orbit normal forms, stabilizers, components and specializations for the full Ore locus remain to be described.
scope.non_domain_boundary: In the secondary n=2 target Q, objects of least period seven or with nonconstant rho_i must have zero divisors. Their existence, projection degeneracy and automatic domainness remain open. This statement is specific to n=2 and is not contradicted by the n=1 domain counterexample with alternating rho. Nonstandard numerical types in Q have been excluded by TYPE-EXHAUST.
scope.domain_regularity_criterion: For a chosen word-homogeneous quadratic presentation of any A in Q, A is a Z-domain if and only if the jump-2, word-length-one generators z_i are left and right regular for i=0,...,6. Each regularity condition concerns multiplication in every degree. Seven-periodicity reduces the indices, not the degrees, so this is not a finite-degree computational test.
scope.pure_degree_one_dichotomy: For every A in Q, without a domain assumption, the excess-zero pure jump-1 subalgebra B has a length-at-most-two simple resolution and endpoint recurrence. Seven-step monodromy first gives the alternative r_2(i)=1 for every i or width at most 13. The finite-width alternative is subsequently excluded by OUTER-RELATION-RANKS; it is no longer an open AS locus.
scope.indexed_isomorphism_criterion: For established domain Ore data (r,S,M,c,L) and (r_prime,S_prime,M_prime,c_prime,L_prime), set T=M S^(-1), J=c^(-1) M^2 S^(-3), lambda=c/c_prime and P_i=T_prime^(-i) P T^i. Bare indexed-isomorphism existence is equivalent to existence of P in GL_2(k) and kappa in k^* satisfying J_prime P=P J, (P tensor P_1)r in k^* r_prime, L_prime P_3=kappa L and L_prime P_4=kappa lambda L. This assumes valid AS/domain Ore data and is not an AS-regularity test or a description of all nonlinear isomorphisms.
scope.diagonal_indexed_classification: For the normalized diagonal quantum three-torus of parameters (a,b,c), bare indexed isomorphism classes are precisely the orbits of the involution (a,b,c)->(a^(-1),b^(-1),c*a^3/b^2). All special values are included; its fixed locus is a=1 and b=+/-1 with c arbitrary nonzero. The finite quotient has dimension 3. This classifies the diagonal family, not the whole domain Ore locus or Q.
scope.outer_relation_ranks: Over the standing algebraically closed field, every A in Q has r_2(i)=r_5(i)=1 and dim B_{i,i+n}=n+1 for its pure jump-1 subalgebra B. This needs neither domainness nor noetherianity. Zero-relation edges in the hypothetical finite-width branch split tensor chains into blocks with at most one two-dimensional relation space; nonzero product covectors extend across the remaining one-dimensional constraints and contradict finite width. Domainness of B or A does not follow from this result alone. MIXED-RELATION-RANKS separately fixes the remaining relation counts.
scope.mixed_relation_ranks: For all Q, r_3(i)=r_4(i)=2. Positivity of the folded Hilbert matrix and divergence of its pure jump-1 part force det P(1,v) identically zero. Its first coefficient forces sum_i(r_3(i)-2)=0; a weight-four cubic-syzygy bound forces r_3(i)+r_3(i+1)<=5. An exact integer check of det P(1,1) over the 890 arrays delta in {-2,-1,0,1,2}^7 with sum zero and delta_i+delta_(i+1)<=1 leaves only delta=0. All assumptions and the matrix orientation are proved before enumeration. Neither projection nondegeneracy nor regularity of z_i is inferred from the ranks.
scope.general_indexed_target: For n>=1 over the standing algebraically closed characteristic-zero field: positive connected locally finite word-quadratic Z-domains with primitive jumps (1^n,2,3), two-sided AS dimension n+2, finitely generated finite projective resolutions of simples, and polynomial row/column growth. No standard Hilbert, noetherian, Koszul or period-one assumption is built into this target.
scope.general_indexed_descent: Universal all-n ordinary descent is false at n1, with exact criterion alpha^2=c beta^2 there. Every n2,n3 domain target descends. At n4, A period one is equivalent to word-Koszulity, N6, B period one and uniform or standard pure-base Hilbert rows. These equivalent conditions are not proved automatic. General descent conditions remain unresolved for n>=5.
scope.general_indexed_ore: Unconditional indexed two-step Ore exhaustion is proved for n=1,2,3 under the original AS/domain/growth hypotheses. For all n, GEN-AS-BASE-ORE proves it from the sole extra AS condition on the pure jump-one base B and its finite two-sided resolutions; no Koszul/H/noetherian/initial-rank/period-one assumptions are added. N3-INDEXED-ORE derives B-AS3 using PERIOD2-BASE-AS3. N3-GRADED-DESCENT further proves final A period one and ordinary graded two-step Ore for all n3 objects. The remaining unconditional range is n>=4.
scope.general_indexed_counterexample: The choice (c,alpha,beta)=(1,1,0) in N1-INDEXED-CLASSIFICATION gives epsilon_(2j)=1 and epsilon_(2j+1)=0, with relations z_i x_(i+2)=x_i z_(i+1), w_i z_(i+3)=z_i w_(i+2), and w_i x_(i+3)=x_i w_(i+1)+epsilon_i z_i z_(i+2). It is a word-Koszul, left/right noetherian AS3 Z-domain with AS translation 6, standard two-variable Hilbert series and least positive period 2. The zz-projection rank of R_4 alternates, obstructing period one and hence any presentation as check(D) for a single graded D.
scope.general_indexed_translation: AS Frobenius duality gives a translation i->i+L and a word-preserving A isomorphic to A(L) for arbitrary n, without assuming Koszulity. Directed reachability identifies the vertex order, and E^1,E^2 with their product recover the quadratic presentation. This does not determine L=n+5 or prove word-Koszulity.
scope.general_normal_z_conditional: For arbitrary n, all r3=n,r5=1 and regular z imply a regular normal z family and A(2) isomorphic to A. Domain gives only r3<=n,r5<=1,r6=0. Attainment is unconditional for n1,n2,n3, and is proved for n4 under any condition in N4-EQUIVALENT-CRITERIA. Ordinary word-Koszul objects also attain the bounds in every n. Do not infer their automaticity for general indexed n>=4.
scope.one_heavy_frobenius_conditional: Indexed non-Koszul one-heavy lemma: Q=T_Z(V direct_sum kw)/(R direct_sum S), V jump one, w jump d>1, R pure V and S in Vw direct_sum wV. If Q is AS(n+1) and B=T_Z(V)/(R) itself is ASn with finite two-sided AS resolutions, then Q=B[w;mu] for an isomorphism B(d)->B. No Koszul, noetherian, prescribed Hilbert or Q-domain assumption. The full Yoneda algebra and its internal degrees, not only the quadratic dual, are used.
scope.one_light_indexed_ore: Every object of Q_1^dom admits a two-step indexed Ore presentation without extra Hilbert, noetherian or Koszul assumptions. AS3 and word-quadraticity force top word length 3 and word-Koszulity; domainness gives r_2=r_6=0; AS duality forces translation 6 and r_3=r_4=r_5=1. The top tensor forces both mixed coefficients of R_4 to be nonzero, and Euler Hilbert series plus ordered spanning gives a PBW basis. Standard Hilbert series and left/right noetherianity are conclusions.
scope.one_light_indexed_classification: Every Q_1^dom object has a normalized presentation z_i x_(i+2)=x_i z_(i+1), w_i z_(i+3)=c z_i w_(i+2), w_i x_(i+3)=x_i w_(i+1)+d_i z_i z_(i+2), where c is nonzero, d_(2j)=c^(-j) alpha and d_(2j+1)=c^(-j) beta. Every parameter triple gives a word-Koszul, left/right noetherian AS3 Z-domain with standard Hilbert series, verified using explicit left/right resolutions. Bare indexed isomorphism is equivalent to c_prime=c and (alpha_prime,beta_prime)=s(alpha,beta) for a nonzero scalar s. For each c the SET of classes is {0} disjoint_union P^1(k), without an affine-quotient or moduli-space assertion. Period one holds exactly when alpha^2=c beta^2, including the zero pair; otherwise the least positive period is two.
scope.three_light_numerics: For every Q_3^dom, top word length N=5, AS translation L=8, word-Koszulity, all relation counts (3,3,3,1,0), H_i(u,t)=1/((1-ut)^3(1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)), regular normal z and A(2) isomorphic to A are proved without extra H/noetherian/Koszul/period assumptions. The pure jump-one domain B has two-sided linear (1,3,3,1) resolutions and H_B=(1-t)^(-3), and PERIOD2-BASE-AS3 separately proves its AS3 property; this is not inferred from numerical ranks alone.
scope.as_base_ore_conditional: For every Q_n^dom, if the pure jump-one subalgebra B itself is ASn with finite two-sided AS resolutions, then r_3=r_4=n, r_5=1, r_6=0 and A is an indexed two-step Ore extension of B. B has period one. For its AS index L_B, one has N_A=L_B+2, L_A=L_B+5 and H_A(u,t)=H_B0(ut)/((1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)). A is word-Koszul iff B is Koszul. Even L_B implies period one of A. General noetherianity or unconditional B-AS is not claimed.
scope.general_r5_growth: For a word-quadratic positive Z-algebra with r_6=0, L-periodic r_5 and polynomial row growth: if 3 does not divide L, r_5(i)+r_5(i-3)>0 and at least ceil(L/2) positions are nonzero. If 3 divides L, at least ceil(L/6) positions are nonzero. In a domain r_5<=1, so the position bounds are sum bounds. The monomial quotient test alone does not exclude alternating missing R5 for L=2; no AS-domain realization of that pattern is asserted.
scope.period_two_base_recognition: Any positive connected locally finite, adjacent-generated quadratic Z-domain with an algebra period B(2) isomorphic to B and dim B_(i,i+m)=binom(m+2,2) is two-sided Koszul and AS-regular of global dimension three with AS translation +3. Koszulity, finite global dimension, noetherianity and period one are not assumed. Quadratic presentation/Hilbert/domain give exact 1331 complexes. The two-vertex fold embeds faithfully in a fraction division category; all rank-(2,2) top tensors are excluded by dimensions of alternating products and rational-function pole growth. Nondegenerate top pairings and the Koszul bimodule resolution give AS duality and global dimension for all unital modules. No ordinary classification is used.
scope.three_light_indexed_ore: Every Q_3^dom admits C=B[z;sigma], A=C[w;theta,delta] as indexed Ore extensions, with sigma:B(2)->B and theta:C(3)->C isomorphisms. B is a quadratic AS3 Z-domain and has period one; A has period two and AS translation eight. Relations are z_i v=sigma_i(v)z_(i+1), w_i v=mu_i(v)w_(i+1)+L_i(v)z_i z_(i+2), w_i z_(i+3)=c_i z_i w_(i+2), with sigma_i,mu_i invertible and c_i nonzero. Ordered B z^a w^b components form PBW bases. No extra H/noetherian/Koszul/period assumption. N3-GRADED-DESCENT separately proves final A period one; full indexed orbit classification remains open.
scope.three_light_derivation_support: In the n3 indexed Ore presentation, either all L_i vanish or all are nonzero. Applying delta to the base relations and using their full left/right support makes L_i=0 equivalent to L_(i+1)=0. In the all-zero case w is a regular normal family, so periods three/two give final A period one. N3-GRADED-DESCENT also settles the all-nonzero branch through extension of the coefficient shift operator.
scope.three_light_graded_descent: Every Q_3^dom is word-preservingly period one and A is isomorphic to check(D), D=B_prime[z;sigma_prime][w;tau_prime,delta_prime], with B_prime an ordinary three-generator quadratic AS3 domain. In a common frame zv=S(v)z, w_i v=S(v)w_(i+1)+ell_i(v)zz, wz=zw, the space E=span ell_i has a well-defined invertible T ell_i=ell_(i+1), T^2=S*|E. T is induced by a base automorphism P commuting with S. Dimensions E0,E1,E3 are direct; E2 reduces to reciprocal distinct eigenvalues or a Jordan block at one. The latter uses the canonical unipotent square root; the former normalizes the relation space explicitly, including resonance cases. Descent gives R_prime=(id tensor P)R, sigma_prime=SP^(-2), tau_prime|V=SP^(-3), tau_prime(z)=z, delta_prime(v)=(ell_0 P^(-3))(v)z^2, delta_prime(z)=0. B_prime is a Zhang twist of the common-frame B0, not necessarily graded-isomorphic to it. No H/Koszul/noetherian/period assumption is added. No least-period-two n3 objects exist in this target. This is an exhaustion theorem, not full orbit classification.
scope.three_light_noetherian: Every Q_3^dom is left/right noetherian in the row/column sense. The ordinary descended first stage C_prime=B_prime[z;sigma_prime] is generated in word degree one. Rogalski-Zhang arXiv1101.1998v2 Lemma1.3(a), applied in that word grading, gives its noetherianity. The automorphism Ore Hilbert basis theorem gives D=C_prime[w;tau_prime,delta_prime] left/right noetherian. The regular graded D modules correspond to representable row/column modules of check(D). This is a conclusion, not a new hypothesis; no arbitrary-dimensional-base noetherianity assertion is made.
scope.four_light_top_excess: Every Q4dom object has top excess D=L-N=3. If D>=4, the excess-zero bar complex gives pure-base simple projective dimensions at most three, excluded by PERIODIC-PD3-OBSTRUCTION. N=6 and L=9 are not unconditional conclusions.
scope.periodic_pd3_obstruction: A positive connected locally finite adjacent quadratic Z-domain with m>=4 generators at each vertex, an actual finite algebra period, polynomial row growth, and finitely generated simple resolutions cannot have every right simple projective dimension at most three. No AS, Koszul or noetherian assumption. A balanced-graph square identity forces the simple Euler eigenvalue negative near u=1, contrary to entrywise nonnegative inverse Hilbert matrices.
scope.four_light_pure_resolution: For Q4dom, s=N-2>=4,L=s+5. Pure B has simple resolution P_(i+s)^q_i -> direct_sum_(j=3..s-1) P_(i+j)^p_ij -> P_(i+2)^r_i -> P_(i+1)^4 -> P_i -> S_i, with q_i=r5(i+s) in {0,1}, not all zero. All ranks are L-periodic. r_i=3+sum_j p_ij-q_i and sum_(i,j)(j-2)p_ij-(s-2)sum_i q_i=2L. No B-AS4 assertion.
scope.four_light_koszul_base: For Q4dom with word-Koszulity, equivalently N6, s4/L9. Pure B has two-sided linear 14641 resolutions, r2=6,r5=1 and all H_B=(1-u)^-4. A Perron-Frobenius spectral-radius crossing excludes any missing q_i. These numerical data do not alone imply B-AS4.
scope.four_light_koszul_numerics: For Q4dom with word-Koszulity, all ranks are (6,4,4,1,0), L9, H_A(u,t)=1/((1-ut)^4(1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)), z is a regular normal family, and A is word-preservingly period one. For alpha_i=4-r3_i>=0, P=F K F and det K(1,v)=-9(sum alpha_i)v+O(v^2); a nonzero defect would bound the Hilbert pole by two, contrary to its pure-base pole four. No B-AS/noetherian/initial-H/period hypothesis.
scope.four_light_equivalent_criteria: Within Q4dom ten conditions are equivalent: A word-Koszul; N6; A period one; B period one; H_i^B independent of i; all H_i^B=(1-u)^-4; B two-sided AS4; A indexed two-step Ore over its AS4 pure B; A is check of ordinary two-step Ore over a four-generator Koszul AS4 domain; all r3(i)=4,r5(i)=1. The rank condition is equivalent to B-AS4 by INDEXED-NORMAL-Z-ORE. The previous numerical implications combine with the noetherian-free ordinary Ore theorem, while B-AS4 implies B period one by GEN-AS-BASE-ORE. Their automaticity remains open. In the Koszul/standard branch base-AS and second Ore are fully proved, without noetherianity.
scope.ordinary_koszul_numerics: For ordinary connected graded word-Koszul AS(n+2) domains with primitive generator weights (1^n,2,3), finite finitely generated simple resolutions and polynomial growth, one gets L=n+5, standard bigraded Hilbert/ranks, pure B Koszul of global dimension n and H_B=(1-t)^-n, regular normal z, and first Ore B[z;sigma]. No initial H or noetherian assumption. The scalar Koszul Euler root bound and total binomial Betti counts force the four excess strands. The companion ORDINARY-KOSZUL-ORE theorem proves B-ASn and the second Ore step under exactly the same hypotheses.
scope.ordinary_koszul_noetherian_ore: Under ORDINARY-KOSZUL-ORE, A is left/right noetherian iff B is left/right noetherian: B=A/(z,w), and conversely use the automorphism Ore Hilbert basis theorem. The Ore structure itself needs no noetherian assumption. The n4 noetherian corollary only records this extra property of the base.
scope.four_generator_as_obstruction: Known Rogalski-Sierra arXiv1101.0737v2 Theorem1.1/(1.2), with Theorem1.6, gives ordinary noetherian Koszul domains of global dimension four with linear 14641 resolution and standard H that are not AS-Gorenstein. Thus those pure numerical properties alone do not recognize AS4. The new N4-EQUIVALENT-CRITERIA theorem proves that these examples cannot be pure bases of any Q4dom: their standard H would imply B-AS4. This uses the parent AS/domain hypotheses.
scope.ordinary_koszul_ore: For ordinary connected graded word-Koszul AS(n+2) domains with primitive weights (1^n,2,3), finite finitely generated simple resolutions and polynomial growth, A=B[z;sigma][w;tau,delta], B a Koszul ASn domain. No initial Hilbert or noetherian assumption. R4 degeneracy produces wv=lambda z^2 and vw=lambda c^-2 z^2, hence an alternating bar cycle in every degree in A/(z), contrary to the regular normal word-degree-one quotient theorem. PBW/Hilbert comparison constructs Ore data; two normal quotients prove B-ASn. No general noetherianity conclusion.
scope.indexed_standard_hilbert_ore: For A in Qn_dom, the standard BIGRADED row Hilbert series 1/((1-ut)^n(1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)) imply indexed two-step Ore, B Koszul ASn and period one, and A word-Koszul. No initial B-AS, Koszul, noetherian or A-period-one assumption. Word-degree-two coefficient comparison gives r3=n,r5=1; INDEXED-NORMAL-Z-ORE then proves PBW and base-AS. Standard H_B and AS duality force a linear resolution. This is not a theorem from the univariate weighted Hilbert series alone.
scope.indexed_normal_z_mixed_ranks: For A in Qn_dom with all r3=n,r5=1, both R4 mixed projections are injective and r4=n. Standard H and Koszulity are not required. Bar obstruction gives r4<=n; a two-vertex Golod-Shafarevich determinant and positive eigenvector exclude r4<n. The subsequent INDEXED-NORMAL-Z-ORE theorem proves non-Koszul PBW and B-AS under the same rank hypotheses, using the highest Euler coefficient rather than an extra Hilbert assumption.
scope.indexed_koszul_normal_z_ore: For A in Qn_dom with word-Koszulity and all r3=n,r5=1, the general INDEXED-NORMAL-Z-ORE criterion supplies B-ASn and indexed Ore. A Koszul iff B Koszul; the ordinary B descent and generator bound then give standard bigraded H and L_A=n+5. No initial H/noetherian/B-AS hypothesis. A separate direct Koszul proof is retained in notes: Q=A/(z), its zero-w bar summand proves B Koszul, E(Q)=F direct_sum F eta, the highest w-count is one, and the Frobenius pairing transfers to F. This alternative is not needed for the non-Koszul main criterion.
scope.four_light_pure_euler_obstruction: A fixed s5,N7,L10 pure-Euler formal model with q=1 has nonnegative Betti data, balance/moment identities, det P=(1-u^10)^3(1+u^20), positive inverse-Hilbert coefficients of polynomial growth, common leading Laurent coefficient, all-degree Hopf inequalities and left/right monotonicity, but nonuniform Hilbert rows. An exact integer certificate plus a cofactor-degree bound proves all degrees, not just a finite sample. It is not a constructed algebra, domain or AS parent. Two-period s5 data are separately excluded analytically. The parent-mixed Euler conditions reduce extensions of the displayed pure model to 20 integers; one displayed extension passes first-order tests but has determinant coefficient -942 at v^2 and is excluded. Every extension of this formal pure model to a Q4dom AS-domain is impossible by N4-TOP-WORD-DIVISIBLE-THREE; the formal model and individual pencil obstruction remain useful methodological examples.
scope.indexed_normal_z_ore: For A in Qn_dom, all r3(i)=n,r5(i)=1 imply B two-sided ASn, indexed two-step Ore, r4=n, B period one, L_A=L_B+5, N_A=L_B+2, D3 and H_A=H_B(ut)/((1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)); A word-Koszul iff B Koszul. No specified H, Koszul, noetherian or initial B-AS assumption. The converse B-ASn implies these ranks is GEN-AS-BASE-ORE, so the original all-n structural target is reduced exactly to the two rank conditions. Normal z folds to two vertices and gives an AS quotient Q. Bar plus GS makes mixed relations a full invertible graph. In free-path Ore coordinates Q=F[w;mu]/(R), coefficient ideals I_j=(R,...,mu^j R) stabilize because F2 is finite dimensional. Thus G=H_Q(I-tT) is polynomial in w-count t. AS duality gives invertible leading Euler coefficient P_J(x)=(-1)^d*x^a*Pi*P_0(x^-1)^T. Since P G=I-tT, J+deg_t G=1. J>=1 forces G constant, I_1=I_0, mu R=R and w regular. The second normal quotient gives B-ASn. No non-Koszul PBW gap remains once r3/r5 are known.
scope.as_graph_ore_recognition: Over S=k^m, let F=T_S(V), mu a degree-preserving automorphism permuting vertices, R subset F2, Q=F[w;mu]/(R). Finite finitely generated simple resolutions and a compatible AS perfect pairing with source-independent highest bidegree (a,J) force J1 and mu(R)=R, hence Q=(F/(R))[w;mu] and w is regular. No domain, growth, Koszul, noetherian or specified Hilbert assumption in this lemma. The indexed version uses AS pairing; finite resolution alone is not claimed sufficient for arbitrary matrix Euler series.
scope.general_r5_gs_saturation: A positive connected locally finite word-quadratic Z-domain with jumps (1^n,2,3), an actual word-preserving period L and polynomial row growth has all r5(i)=1 if 3 does not divide L. If 3 divides L, at least one complete residue class modulo three has r5=1 everywhere. No AS, finite global dimension, Koszul or noetherian assumption. The two-stage matrix GS inequality is evaluated on a=eps^2/(1-eps^2), b=eps, c=1-eps^2. Orbit-mean deficit gives a positive left vector and a negative first-order product unless one orbit is saturated. The other two classes and r3=n are not concluded. In Q4dom this saturation is used in N4-TOP-WORD-DIVISIBLE-THREE to rule out every hypothetical AS shift L not divisible by three.
scope.four_light_top_word_divisibility: Every Q4dom object has 3 dividing N and L=N+3. No initial Koszul, Hilbert, noetherian or period-one assumption. If 3 does not divide L, R5 GS gives all r5=1. Nonzero w powers force det P(eps^2,eps^-1)=0; its simple-kernel coefficients give sum r4=4L and sum r3=sum p_(s-1). Pure/mixed moments force third pure Tor into word s-1. Domain cancellation and minimal exactness give each tail rank p_i>=2, so s<=6. The s5 and s6 numerical Euler matrices have positive roots inside the unit disk, contradicting polynomial growth. Hence the only unresolved non-Koszul top words are N=9,12,15,...; first N9/L12/s7. This is an analytic proof with no enumeration. The N7 ten-period formal model has no AS-domain parent extension.
scope.nozz_koszul_structure: For any Qn_dom, add word-Koszulity and zero projection of every R4 to zz for the fixed word grading. Then all r3=r4=n,r5=1, B Koszul ASn, standard bigraded Hilbert and L=n+5 hold. Both z and w are regular normal families, giving actual periods 2 and 3 and hence period one; A descends to an ordinary two-step skew polynomial algebra B0[z;sigma][w;tau]. Finite folded Frobenius duality yields E=F+Fzeta+Feta+Fzetaeta as a direct sum of multidegrees, equal dimensions of F and E11, and injective right multiplication by zetaeta and etazeta. This forces the ranks without assuming them. No initial H, noetherian or period-one assumption. The no-zz hypothesis is additional, invariant under fixed-word/jump-preserving generator basis changes only.
scope.one_heavy_periodic_gs: For a positive connected locally finite word-quadratic periodic Z-algebra generated by n adjacent V arrows and one jump-h arrow y, with only VV and Vy/yV relations, no yy relations, mixed rank at most n and polynomial row growth, at least one complete +h orbit has all mixed ranks n. If gcd(h,L)=1 all mixed ranks are n. No AS, domain, Koszul, noetherian or finite global dimension assumption. The compressed first GS coefficient is a negative weighted cyclic shift if every orbit has a deficit; a positive left vector and first-order correction contradict P2 H>=I.
scope.nozz_periodic_structure: For any Qn_dom with zero R4-to-zz projections and an actual word-preserving period L not divisible by six, all r3=r4=n,r5=1 and full indexed Ore over an ASn base follow without Koszulity. All r5=1 follows from NOZZ-FULL-R5 and is not an extra assumption. One-heavy GS on A/(w),A/(z) gives normal z,w, periods two,three and ordinary two-step skew descent. For 6|L, full r5 still follows but full r3 is not proved here. At n4 a nonKoszul nozz object could only have N=9,15,21,...; existence remains unproved. No general assertion of standard Hilbert, Koszulity or noetherianity.
scope.matrix_generator_bound_obstruction: The explicit formal 2x2 Euler matrix with q=(1-t)^2, diagonals q^2+a^2t^2,q^2 and off-diagonals -atq has AS-type degree-four reciprocity, nonnegative Betti signs, det=(1-t)^8 and entrywise nonnegative polynomial-growth inverse. Its generator matrix has Perron root 4+a>4. This is not a realized algebra and fails domain leading-Laurent component comparison, since diagonal pole orders differ. Thus those formal Euler conditions alone do not prove a matrix generator bound.
scope.koszul_dual_quotient_support: For any word-Koszul Qn_dom, its finite folded Ext algebra E has the heavy dual zeta normal in the sense E zeta=zeta E. Domain mixed projections yield eta X subset X eta+S zeta^2 S and the reverse inclusion. With eta^2=0, E/(zeta)=Fbar+Fbar eta has excess support only 0 and 2. No nozz, r5 saturation, H, noetherian or period-one assumption. This does not assert a normalizing automorphism for the zero-divisor zeta.
scope.indexed_koszul_ore: Every word-Koszul Qn_dom, for arbitrary n>=1, has all r3=r4=n,r5=1, a Koszul ASn pure base B, full indexed two-step Ore structure, D3,N=n+2,L=n+5 and standard bigraded row Hilbert series. No additional H/noetherian/nozz/period-one/mixed-rank hypothesis. GS gives r5 not identically zero and D>=3. The AS complement of any pure element annihilating zeta lies in zeta E, proving F->F zeta injective and r3=n. If eta zeta=0, its complement is killed by the quotient support unless D4. At D4, F^(d-2) pairs with E^2_e4=R6*=0, hence vanishes, so the quotient component (d-1,2)=Fbar^(d-2) eta is zero as well; the complement again lies in zeta E and gives a contradiction. Thus all r5=1 and the existing rank criterion applies. No exceptional Koszul dimension remains. Unrestricted non-Koszul objects are not settled.
scope.indexed_koszul_even_descent: For every word-Koszul Qn_dom with n even, normal-z period two and odd AS period L=n+5 combine to give actual word-preserving period one and ordinary graded two-step Ore descent over a Koszul ASn domain. No noetherian assumption. Universal odd-n descent is not concluded and is false at n1.
scope.nonkoszul_examples_and_existence: No nonKoszul example satisfying all Qn_dom hypotheses has been constructed, and none was found in the primary sources checked in this update; this is not a complete nonexistence or literature-exhaustion result. At n4, N9,12,... are unexcluded top-word possibilities, not realized families. The classical quadratic Heisenberg U(h2) is a noetherian domain, AS5 with four minimal generators, H=(1-t)^-4(1-t^2)^-1 and minimal shifts 0,1,2,4,5,6 (Floystad-Vatne arXiv0911.5129v3 Theorem2.1/Remark3.2). It is nonKoszul but misses generatorcount=ASdim. Its quadratic dual has H=1+4t+5t^2 while full Ext has higher generators. For any finite-dimensional positively graded Lie g, augmentation indecomposables are g/[g,g], so ASdim-minus-minimalgen equals dim[g,g]; only abelian enveloping algebras satisfy equality. These are known-example and elementary comparison statements, not a new target counterexample.
scope.d3_exact_boundary_kernel: For Qn_dom with D3 and a word-preserving period L divisible by three, the heavy-w boundary P(epsilon^2,epsilon^-1) has strictly positive right and left kernels in K=ker(I-S^3) for each fixed 0<epsilon<1, satisfying h_i>=epsilon h_(i+2), g_(i+2)>=epsilon g_i. Rational leading Laurent coefficients of H(epsilon^2/c,c/epsilon) at c1 give normalized rational kernels analytic at epsilon0, even when the boundary kernel has higher dimension. This does not say that K is invariant under P or determine the Hilbert pole order.
scope.local_square_r5_obstruction: For a word-quadratic Z-domain with Tor3(word3,excess4)=0, a relation w_i v=z_i z_(i+2) forces t_i t_(i+2)=0, and x w_(i+1)=z_i z_(i+2) forces t_(i-3)t_(i-1)=0. If b_i=n+1 both constraints hold. Cancellation creates another quadratic relation and a nonzero (R tensor W) intersection (W tensor R) in the forbidden bidegree. D3 ensures the vanishing hypothesis.
scope.single_z_collapse: For any quadratic Z-domain with primitive jumps (1^n,2,3), t_(i+3k)=0 and t_(i+2+3k)=1 for 0<=k<M, and b_(i+3k)=n+1 for 0<=k<=M, imply M+1<=n. The result also holds after interchanging zero and one in the first two hypotheses. The M+1 one-z words are independent in defect degree one; common z multiplication is injective, and maximal R4 rank compresses the images into w^(M+1)V of dimension at most n. No AS, growth or period hypothesis.
scope.d3_two_saturated_classes: For Qn_dom with D3 and 3|L, at least two full mod-three classes have t_i=r5(i)=1 at every position. If exactly r,r+1 are saturated, b_i=r4(i)=n pointwise on class r+1. If all r5=1, then every b_i<=n and one entire class has b_i=n. Applies unconditionally to every Q4dom for every N, not only N9. Pointwise boundary equations, cubic obstruction, defect propagation and the finite single-z collapse exclude the one-saturated class and the indicated two-saturated deficit. Full r5 and all r3 remain unproved.
scope.euler_mahler_face_factors: For a word-graded positive locally finite Z-algebra with primitive jumps (1^n,2,3), actual word-preserving period L, finite finitely generated simple resolutions and polynomial row growth, m(detP)=0. If all pure w products are nonzero, let g=gcd(L,3): detP_B(u) and (1-(uv^2)^(L/g))^g divide detP(u,v) in Z[u,v]; they are coprime so their product divides. The proof uses integer constant term one and analytic Hilbert inverses, the established Issa-Lalin Theorem1.2(s1), and a proved Jensen equality face lemma. Parity under (x,y)->(-x,-y) gives polynomial rather than Laurent descent. No AS reciprocity, Koszulity or noetherianity is required after the explicit hypotheses. Factor multiplicity does not determine boundary corank.
scope.nozz_full_r5: For a quadratic Z-domain with primitive jumps (1^n,2,3), actual word-preserving period L and polynomial row growth, zero projection of all R4 to zz forces every r5=1. In A/(V) the partial wz->zw scalar relations have no overlaps; one missing position yields two equal-jump normal words whose arbitrary concatenations give exponential growth. No AS, finite global dimension, Koszulity, noetherianity or divisibility restriction on L.
scope.d3_two_saturated_leading: In the D3 two-saturated branch with classes0,1 full and class2 not full, positive analytic exact-K kernels necessarily have leading supports h(0)=e2 and g(0)=e1 after normalization. With h2=g1=1, h0=kappa epsilon+...,h1=nu epsilon^2+...,g0=lambda epsilon+...,g2=mu epsilon^2+..., with nu>=kappa>=1 and mu>=lambda>=1. Any positive leading class0 coordinate forces maximal b on a whole class and violates the forward or reverse finite single-z lemma. No corank-one or Hilbert pole-order conclusion.
scope.d3_full_r5_moment: For Qn_dom with D3, L=3ell>=9 and all r5=1, put a_i=r3(i),b_i=r4(i),H_i=Tor3(word3,excess3) dimension. Then sum(a_i-H_i)+sum(b_i-n)=0. Exact full-matrix trace calculation yields x^3 coefficient y^(2ell-1)/(1-y^(2ell)) times that sum in detP(x^2,y/x)/(1-y^(2ell))^3; the face-factor theorem forces the coefficient polynomial. No classwise constancy of b_i is assumed. For n4, H_i=p_(i+6,N-3). This is a necessary identity, not automatic Koszulity.
scope.four_light_cubic_corner_bounds: For Q4dom, h_j=p_(j+6,N-3)=dim diagonal E3_excess3 at j, u_j=t_(j+1)a_j, v_j=t_j a_(j+3), h_j<=min(b_j,b_(j+2),u_j+v_j,1+min(u_j,v_j)). Both neighboring t zero imply h=0; one zero implies h<=1. Thus q_i=1,t_(i+N-3)=0 forces a nonzero lower-word pure third syzygy. Also dim diagonal E3_excess2 at j <=min(r_j+a_j,r_(j+3)+a_(j+2)); equality forces injectivity and a direct sum in the displayed normal form. Uses the quadratic-dual diagonal subalgebra, never generation of full Ext in degree one.

claims.scope: All Q without domain assumptions: either every r_2(i)=1 with pure jump-1 dimensions n+1, or the pure jump-1 subalgebra has width at most 13. The proof uses excess-zero bar complexes, endpoint Hilbert recurrences and two actual independent solution vectors to control every seven-step monodromy mode. This intermediate dichotomy is strengthened by OUTER-RELATION-RANKS, which excludes the finite-width branch.

Over the standing algebraically closed field, every A in Q has r_2(i)=r_5(i)=1 and dim B_{i,i+n}=n+1 for its pure jump-1 subalgebra B. This needs neither domainness nor noetherianity. Zero-relation edges in the hypothetical finite-width branch split tensor chains into blocks with at most one two-dimensional relation space; nonzero product covectors extend across the remaining one-dimensional constraints and contradict finite width. Domainness of B or A does not follow from this result alone. MIXED-RELATION-RANKS separately fixes the remaining relation counts.

For all Q, r_3(i)=r_4(i)=2. Positivity of the folded Hilbert matrix and divergence of its pure jump-1 part force det P(1,v) identically zero. Its first coefficient forces sum_i(r_3(i)-2)=0; a weight-four cubic-syzygy bound forces r_3(i)+r_3(i+1)<=5. An exact integer check of det P(1,1) over the 890 arrays delta in {-2,-1,0,1,2}^7 with sum zero and delta_i+delta_(i+1)<=1 leaves only delta=0. All assumptions and the matrix orientation are proved before enumeration. Neither projection nondegeneracy nor regularity of z_i is inferred from the ranks.

Every A in Q has standard relation counts (1,2,2,1,0), standard word-Koszul resolutions and the prescribed two-variable Hilbert series, so Q=H=S. The proof uses the exact finite-computation theorem for the mixed ranks and coefficientwise uniqueness of the Euler recurrences. This completes numerical type exhaustion, not domainness, period-one exhaustion or the full indexed-isomorphism classification.

For established domain Ore data (r,S,M,c,L) and (r_prime,S_prime,M_prime,c_prime,L_prime), set T=M S^(-1), J=c^(-1) M^2 S^(-3), lambda=c/c_prime and P_i=T_prime^(-i) P T^i. Bare indexed-isomorphism existence is equivalent to existence of P in GL_2(k) and kappa in k^* satisfying J_prime P=P J, (P tensor P_1)r in k^* r_prime, L_prime P_3=kappa L and L_prime P_4=kappa lambda L. This assumes valid AS/domain Ore data and is not an AS-regularity test or a description of all nonlinear isomorphisms.

Complete bare indexed-isomorphism existence for all normalized diagonal quantum parameters: equality or the involution (a,b,c)->(a^(-1),b^(-1),c*a^3/b^2), including coincident eigenvalues and all special parameters. No generic-parameter exclusion.

The diagonal quantum indexed-class space is the finite order-two quotient of (k^*)^3 by the stated involution and has dimension 3. Fixed locus: a=1, b=+/-1, c arbitrary nonzero. This is a statement about the diagonal family, not the global AS moduli space.

For all Q, if R_5(p)=k(z_p w_(p+2)) and R_5(m)=k(w_m z_(m+3)), then m-p is not 2,3,4 modulo 7. Distances 2 and 4 create forbidden cubic syzygies; distance 3 yields an exponentially growing monomial quotient. This does not exclude a single one-sided relation or establish AS examples for allowed configurations.

Every object of Q_1^dom admits a two-step indexed Ore presentation without extra Hilbert, noetherian or Koszul assumptions. AS3 and word-quadraticity force top word length 3 and word-Koszulity; domainness gives r_2=r_6=0; AS duality forces translation 6 and r_3=r_4=r_5=1. The top tensor forces both mixed coefficients of R_4 to be nonzero, and Euler Hilbert series plus ordered spanning gives a PBW basis. Standard Hilbert series and left/right noetherianity are conclusions.

Every Q_1^dom object has a normalized presentation z_i x_(i+2)=x_i z_(i+1), w_i z_(i+3)=c z_i w_(i+2), w_i x_(i+3)=x_i w_(i+1)+d_i z_i z_(i+2), where c is nonzero, d_(2j)=c^(-j) alpha and d_(2j+1)=c^(-j) beta. Every parameter triple gives a word-Koszul, left/right noetherian AS3 Z-domain with standard Hilbert series, verified using explicit left/right resolutions. Bare indexed isomorphism is equivalent to c_prime=c and (alpha_prime,beta_prime)=s(alpha,beta) for a nonzero scalar s. For each c the SET of classes is {0} disjoint_union P^1(k), without an affine-quotient or moduli-space assertion. Period one holds exactly when alpha^2=c beta^2, including the zero pair; otherwise the least positive period is two.

The choice (c,alpha,beta)=(1,1,0) in N1-INDEXED-CLASSIFICATION gives epsilon_(2j)=1 and epsilon_(2j+1)=0, with relations z_i x_(i+2)=x_i z_(i+1), w_i z_(i+3)=z_i w_(i+2), and w_i x_(i+3)=x_i w_(i+1)+epsilon_i z_i z_(i+2). It is a word-Koszul, left/right noetherian AS3 Z-domain with AS translation 6, standard two-variable Hilbert series and least positive period 2. The zz-projection rank of R_4 alternates, obstructing period one and hence any presentation as check(D) for a single graded D. Therefore universal arbitrary-n graded two-step Ore descent is false. This special case of the complete n=1 classification does not refute indexed Ore exhaustion and is not an n>=3 counterexample.

AS Frobenius duality gives a translation i->i+L and a word-preserving A isomorphic to A(L) for arbitrary n, without assuming Koszulity. Directed reachability identifies the vertex order, and E^1,E^2 with their product recover the quadratic presentation. This does not determine L=n+5 or prove word-Koszulity.

For arbitrary n, if all r_3(i)=n and r_5(i)=1 and all z_i are left/right regular, the mixed relation projections are isomorphisms, the z_i form a regular normal family, and A(2) is isomorphic to A. Domainness alone gives r_3<=n, r_5<=1 and r_6=0. Attainment of the upper bounds is proved for n=1,2,3 but not established unconditionally for n>=4.

Indexed non-Koszul one-heavy lemma: Q=T_Z(V direct_sum kw)/(R direct_sum S), V jump one, w jump d>1, R pure V and S in Vw direct_sum wV. For a word-quadratic positive Z-algebra with r_6=0, L-periodic r_5 and polynomial row growth: if 3 does not divide L, r_5(i)+r_5(i-3)>0 and at least ceil(L/2) positions are nonzero. If 3 divides L, at least ceil(L/6) positions are nonzero. In a domain r_5<=1, so the position bounds are sum bounds. The monomial quotient test alone does not exclude alternating missing R5 for L=2; no AS-domain realization of that pattern is asserted.

A positive periodic jump-one Z-domain with m>=3 generators and polynomial row growth cannot have every simple projective dimension at most two. Row Hilbert ratios tend to one; the Euler limit forces r_i=m-1 and hence an interior pole.

For a periodic three-generator jump-one Z-domain with simple resolutions (1,3,r_i,q_i), shifts (0,1,2,s), q_i in {0,1}, period L=s+5 and polynomial growth, s=3, r_i=3, q_i=1. The folded Hilbert leading coefficient is cJ with pole order at least two. Two Laurent identities leave only the standard case or s9/L14; the latter has det P7=(1-u^7)^2(1-64u^7) and is excluded. This does not itself prove AS-Gorensteinness.

For every Q_3^dom, top word length N=5, AS translation L=8, word-Koszulity, all relation counts (3,3,3,1,0), H_i(u,t)=1/((1-ut)^3(1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)), regular normal z and A(2) isomorphic to A are proved without extra H/noetherian/Koszul/period assumptions. The pure jump-one domain B has two-sided linear (1,3,3,1) resolutions and H_B=(1-t)^(-3), and PERIOD2-BASE-AS3 separately proves its AS3 property; this is not inferred from numerical ranks alone.

For every Q_n^dom, if the pure jump-one subalgebra B itself is ASn with finite two-sided AS resolutions, then r_3=r_4=n, r_5=1, r_6=0 and A is an indexed two-step Ore extension of B. General noetherianity or unconditional B-AS is not claimed.

A positive two-periodic Z-domain of polynomial growth folds to a two-object category whose nonzero morphisms admit faithful localization. Corner polynomial-growth domains are Ore because disjoint principal ideals would produce exponential binary-word growth. Nonzero return arrows supply common multiples for different targets. A nonzero arrow frame puts X,Y in one division ring while preserving all alternating products and dimensions.

Any positive connected locally finite, adjacent-generated quadratic Z-domain with an algebra period B(2) isomorphic to B and dim B_(i,i+m)=binom(m+2,2) is two-sided Koszul and AS-regular of global dimension three with AS translation +3. Koszulity, finite global dimension, noetherianity and period one are not assumed. Quadratic presentation/Hilbert/domain give exact 1331 complexes. The two-vertex fold embeds faithfully in a fraction division category; all rank-(2,2) top tensors are excluded by dimensions of alternating products and rational-function pole growth. Nondegenerate top pairings and the Koszul bimodule resolution give AS duality and global dimension for all unital modules. No ordinary classification is used.

Every Q_3^dom admits C=B[z;sigma], A=C[w;theta,delta] as indexed Ore extensions, with sigma:B(2)->B and theta:C(3)->C isomorphisms. B is a quadratic AS3 Z-domain and has period one; A has period two and AS translation eight. Relations are z_i v=sigma_i(v)z_(i+1), w_i v=mu_i(v)w_(i+1)+L_i(v)z_i z_(i+2), w_i z_(i+3)=c_i z_i w_(i+2), with sigma_i,mu_i invertible and c_i nonzero. Ordered B z^a w^b components form PBW bases. In the n3 indexed Ore presentation, either all L_i vanish or all are nonzero. Applying delta to the base relations and using their full left/right support makes L_i=0 equivalent to L_(i+1)=0. In the all-zero case w is a regular normal family, so periods three/two give final A period one. N3-GRADED-DESCENT also settles the all-nonzero branch through extension of the coefficient shift operator.

Every Q_3^dom is word-preservingly period one and A is isomorphic to check(D), D=B_prime[z;sigma_prime][w;tau_prime,delta_prime], with B_prime an ordinary three-generator quadratic AS3 domain. In a common frame zv=S(v)z, w_i v=S(v)w_(i+1)+ell_i(v)zz, wz=zw, the space E=span ell_i has a well-defined invertible T ell_i=ell_(i+1), T^2=S*|E. T is induced by a base automorphism P commuting with S. Dimensions E0,E1,E3 are direct; E2 reduces to reciprocal distinct eigenvalues or a Jordan block at one. The latter uses the canonical unipotent square root; the former normalizes the relation space explicitly, including resonance cases. Descent gives R_prime=(id tensor P)R, sigma_prime=SP^(-2), tau_prime|V=SP^(-3), tau_prime(z)=z, delta_prime(v)=(ell_0 P^(-3))(v)z^2, delta_prime(z)=0. B_prime is a Zhang twist of the common-frame B0, not necessarily graded-isomorphic to it. No H/Koszul/noetherian/period assumption is added. No least-period-two n3 objects exist in this target. This is an exhaustion theorem, not full orbit classification.

Every Q_3^dom is left/right noetherian in the row/column sense. The ordinary descended first stage C_prime=B_prime[z;sigma_prime] is generated in word degree one. Rogalski-Zhang arXiv1101.1998v2 Lemma1.3(a), applied in that word grading, gives its noetherianity. The automorphism Ore Hilbert basis theorem gives D=C_prime[w;tau_prime,delta_prime] left/right noetherian. The regular graded D modules correspond to representable row/column modules of check(D). This is a conclusion, not a new hypothesis; no arbitrary-dimensional-base noetherianity assertion is made.

A positive connected locally finite adjacent quadratic Z-domain with m>=4 generators at each vertex, an actual finite algebra period, polynomial row growth, and finitely generated simple resolutions cannot have every right simple projective dimension at most three. No AS, Koszul or noetherian assumption. A balanced-graph square identity forces the simple Euler eigenvalue negative near u=1, contrary to entrywise nonnegative inverse Hilbert matrices.

Every Q4dom object has top excess D=L-N=3. If D>=4, the excess-zero bar complex gives pure-base simple projective dimensions at most three, excluded by PERIODIC-PD3-OBSTRUCTION. N=6 and L=9 are not unconditional conclusions.

For Q4dom, s=N-2>=4,L=s+5. Pure B has simple resolution P_(i+s)^q_i -> direct_sum_(j=3..s-1) P_(i+j)^p_ij -> P_(i+2)^r_i -> P_(i+1)^4 -> P_i -> S_i, with q_i=r5(i+s) in {0,1}, not all zero. All ranks are L-periodic. r_i=3+sum_j p_ij-q_i and sum_(i,j)(j-2)p_ij-(s-2)sum_i q_i=2L. No B-AS4 assertion.

For Q4dom with word-Koszulity, equivalently N6, s4/L9. Pure B has two-sided linear 14641 resolutions, r2=6,r5=1 and all H_B=(1-u)^-4. A Perron-Frobenius spectral-radius crossing excludes any missing q_i. These numerical data do not alone imply B-AS4.

For Q4dom with word-Koszulity, all ranks are (6,4,4,1,0), L9, H_A(u,t)=1/((1-ut)^4(1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)), z is a regular normal family, and A is word-preservingly period one. For alpha_i=4-r3_i>=0, P=F K F and det K(1,v)=-9(sum alpha_i)v+O(v^2); a nonzero defect would bound the Hilbert pole by two, contrary to its pure-base pole four. No B-AS/noetherian/initial-H/period hypothesis.

Within Q4dom ten conditions are equivalent: A word-Koszul; N6; A period one; B period one; H_i^B independent of i; all H_i^B=(1-u)^-4; B two-sided AS4; A indexed two-step Ore over its AS4 pure B; A is check of ordinary two-step Ore over a four-generator Koszul AS4 domain; all r3(i)=4,r5(i)=1. The rank condition is equivalent to B-AS4 by INDEXED-NORMAL-Z-ORE. The previous numerical implications combine with the noetherian-free ordinary Ore theorem, while B-AS4 implies B period one by GEN-AS-BASE-ORE. Their automaticity remains open. In the Koszul/standard branch base-AS and second Ore are fully proved, without noetherianity.

For a connected Koszul algebra with n degree-one generators, finite global dimension m, finite Tor and polynomial growth: n<=m, top Betti one; if n=m the Hilbert series is (1-t)^-n and all Betti numbers are binomial. No AS condition; this scalar argument is not an indexed matrix result.

For ordinary connected graded word-Koszul AS(n+2) domains with primitive generator weights (1^n,2,3), finite finitely generated simple resolutions and polynomial growth, one gets L=n+5, standard bigraded Hilbert/ranks, pure B Koszul of global dimension n and H_B=(1-t)^-n, regular normal z, and first Ore B[z;sigma]. No initial H or noetherian assumption. The scalar Koszul Euler root bound and total binomial Betti counts force the four excess strands. The companion ORDINARY-KOSZUL-ORE theorem proves B-ASn and the second Ore step under exactly the same hypotheses.

Under ORDINARY-KOSZUL-ORE, A is left/right noetherian iff B is left/right noetherian: B=A/(z,w), and conversely use the automorphism Ore Hilbert basis theorem. The Ore structure itself needs no noetherian assumption. The n4 noetherian corollary only records this extra property of the base.

For Q4dom under any of the ten equivalent conditions, ordinary two-step Ore and B-AS4 already hold without noetherianity. If the ordinary descent is additionally left/right noetherian, its AS4 base is also left/right noetherian. This property is not asserted automatic.

In a positively connected graded algebra, nonzero degree-one x,y with xy=yx=0 give nonzero Tor_(d,d) for every d via alternating bar tensors. Quadraticity, Koszulity and noetherianity are unnecessary. The relative bar argument also works for composable arrows over finite semisimple degree zero.

For a finite-global-dimension graded domain with regular normal word-degree-one z and wz=c zw, a relation wv=lambda z^2 with v,w nonzero modulo z and lambda nonzero is impossible. Cancellation gives the reversed factorization and the normal quotient contradicts BAR-TWO-CYCLE.

For ordinary connected graded word-Koszul AS(n+2) domains with primitive weights (1^n,2,3), finite finitely generated simple resolutions and polynomial growth, A=B[z;sigma][w;tau,delta], B a Koszul ASn domain. No initial Hilbert or noetherian assumption. R4 degeneracy produces wv=lambda z^2 and vw=lambda c^-2 z^2, hence an alternating bar cycle in every degree in A/(z), contrary to the regular normal word-degree-one quotient theorem. PBW/Hilbert comparison constructs Ore data; two normal quotients prove B-ASn. No general noetherianity conclusion.

For A in Qn_dom, the standard BIGRADED row Hilbert series 1/((1-ut)^n(1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)) imply indexed two-step Ore, B Koszul ASn and period one, and A word-Koszul. No initial B-AS, Koszul, noetherian or A-period-one assumption. Word-degree-two coefficient comparison gives r3=n,r5=1; INDEXED-NORMAL-Z-ORE then proves PBW and base-AS. Standard H_B and AS duality force a linear resolution. This is not a theorem from the univariate weighted Hilbert series alone.

For A in Qn_dom with all r3=n,r5=1, both R4 mixed projections are injective and r4=n. Standard H and Koszulity are not required. Bar obstruction gives r4<=n; a two-vertex Golod-Shafarevich determinant and positive eigenvector exclude r4<n. The subsequent INDEXED-NORMAL-Z-ORE theorem proves non-Koszul PBW and B-AS under the same rank hypotheses, using the highest Euler coefficient rather than an extra Hilbert assumption.

For A in Qn_dom with word-Koszulity and all r3=n,r5=1, the general INDEXED-NORMAL-Z-ORE criterion supplies B-ASn and indexed Ore. A Koszul iff B Koszul; the ordinary B descent and generator bound then give standard bigraded H and L_A=n+5. No initial H/noetherian/B-AS hypothesis. A separate direct Koszul proof is retained in notes: Q=A/(z), its zero-w bar summand proves B Koszul, E(Q)=F direct_sum F eta, the highest w-count is one, and the Frobenius pairing transfers to F. This alternative is not needed for the non-Koszul main criterion.

A fixed s5,N7,L10 pure-Euler formal model with q=1 has nonnegative Betti data, balance/moment identities, det P=(1-u^10)^3(1+u^20), positive inverse-Hilbert coefficients of polynomial growth, common leading Laurent coefficient, all-degree Hopf inequalities and left/right monotonicity, but nonuniform Hilbert rows. An exact integer certificate plus a cofactor-degree bound proves all degrees, not just a finite sample. It is not a constructed algebra, domain or AS parent. Two-period s5 data are separately excluded analytically. The parent-mixed Euler conditions reduce extensions of the displayed pure model to 20 integers; one displayed extension passes first-order tests but has determinant coefficient -942 at v^2 and is excluded. Every extension of this formal pure model to a Q4dom AS-domain is impossible by N4-TOP-WORD-DIVISIBLE-THREE; the formal model and individual pencil obstruction remain useful methodological examples.

For Q4dom, the pure resolution branch s5,N7 cannot have a two-periodic pure B. The two-vertex determinant and unit-circle roots exclude every q0,q1 in {0,1}, not all zero. This numerical two-period obstruction does not itself apply to the ten-period formal model. The separate N4-TOP-WORD-DIVISIBLE-THREE theorem rules out all N7 AS-domain parents and all N not divisible by three.

For the displayed s5 pure formal model, parent AS6 duality and the pure pole of order three force a cubic matrix pencil to be identically singular. A displayed 20-integer mixed extension passes nonnegativity/Segre/first-order constraints but its determinant has v^2 coefficient -942, so it is impossible. This coefficient calculation alone excludes the displayed extension; the separate N4-TOP-WORD-DIVISIBLE-THREE theorem excludes all AS-domain parent extensions.

Over S=k^m, let F=T_S(V), mu a degree-preserving automorphism permuting vertices, R subset F2, Q=F[w;mu]/(R). Finite finitely generated simple resolutions and a compatible AS perfect pairing with source-independent highest bidegree (a,J) force J1 and mu(R)=R, hence Q=(F/(R))[w;mu] and w is regular. No domain, growth, Koszul, noetherian or specified Hilbert assumption in this lemma. The indexed version uses AS pairing; finite resolution alone is not claimed sufficient for arbitrary matrix Euler series.

For A in Qn_dom, all r3(i)=n,r5(i)=1 imply B two-sided ASn, indexed two-step Ore, r4=n, B period one, L_A=L_B+5, N_A=L_B+2, D3 and H_A=H_B(ut)/((1-ut^2)(1-ut^3)); A word-Koszul iff B Koszul. No specified H, Koszul, noetherian or initial B-AS assumption. The converse B-ASn implies these ranks is GEN-AS-BASE-ORE, so the original all-n structural target is reduced exactly to the two rank conditions. Normal z folds to two vertices and gives an AS quotient Q. Bar plus GS makes mixed relations a full invertible graph. In free-path Ore coordinates Q=F[w;mu]/(R), coefficient ideals I_j=(R,...,mu^j R) stabilize because F2 is finite dimensional. Thus G=H_Q(I-tT) is polynomial in w-count t. AS duality gives invertible leading Euler coefficient P_J(x)=(-1)^d*x^a*Pi*P_0(x^-1)^T. Since P G=I-tT, J+deg_t G=1. J>=1 forces G constant, I_1=I_0, mu R=R and w regular. The second normal quotient gives B-ASn. No non-Koszul PBW gap remains once r3/r5 are known.

A positive connected locally finite word-quadratic Z-domain with jumps (1^n,2,3), an actual word-preserving period L and polynomial row growth has all r5(i)=1 if 3 does not divide L. If 3 divides L, at least one complete residue class modulo three has r5=1 everywhere. No AS, finite global dimension, Koszul or noetherian assumption. The two-stage matrix GS inequality is evaluated on a=eps^2/(1-eps^2), b=eps, c=1-eps^2. Orbit-mean deficit gives a positive left vector and a negative first-order product unless one orbit is saturated. The other two classes and r3=n are not concluded. In Q4dom this saturation is used in N4-TOP-WORD-DIVISIBLE-THREE to rule out every hypothetical AS shift L not divisible by three.

Every Q4dom object has 3 dividing N and L=N+3. No initial Koszul, Hilbert, noetherian or period-one assumption. If 3 does not divide L, R5 GS gives all r5=1. Nonzero w powers force det P(eps^2,eps^-1)=0; its simple-kernel coefficients give sum r4=4L and sum r3=sum p_(s-1). Pure/mixed moments force third pure Tor into word s-1. Domain cancellation and minimal exactness give each tail rank p_i>=2, so s<=6. The s5 and s6 numerical Euler matrices have positive roots inside the unit disk, contradicting polynomial growth. Hence the only unresolved non-Koszul top words are N=9,12,15,...; first N9/L12/s7. This is an analytic proof with no enumeration. The N7 ten-period formal model has no AS-domain parent extension.

For any Qn_dom, add word-Koszulity and zero projection of every R4 to zz for the fixed word grading. Then all r3=r4=n,r5=1, B Koszul ASn, standard bigraded Hilbert and L=n+5 hold. Both z and w are regular normal families, giving actual periods 2 and 3 and hence period one; A descends to an ordinary two-step skew polynomial algebra B0[z;sigma][w;tau]. Finite folded Frobenius duality yields E=F+Fzeta+Feta+Fzetaeta as a direct sum of multidegrees, equal dimensions of F and E11, and injective right multiplication by zetaeta and etazeta. This forces the ranks without assuming them. No initial H, noetherian or period-one assumption. The no-zz hypothesis is additional, invariant under fixed-word/jump-preserving generator basis changes only.

For a positive connected locally finite word-quadratic periodic Z-algebra generated by n adjacent V arrows and one jump-h arrow y, with only VV and Vy/yV relations, no yy relations, mixed rank at most n and polynomial row growth, at least one complete +h orbit has all mixed ranks n. If gcd(h,L)=1 all mixed ranks are n. No AS, domain, Koszul, noetherian or finite global dimension assumption. The compressed first GS coefficient is a negative weighted cyclic shift if every orbit has a deficit; a positive left vector and first-order correction contradict P2 H>=I.

For any Qn_dom with zero R4-to-zz projections and an actual word-preserving period L not divisible by six, all r3=r4=n,r5=1 and full indexed Ore over an ASn base follow without Koszulity. All r5=1 follows from NOZZ-FULL-R5 and is not an extra assumption. One-heavy GS on A/(w),A/(z) gives normal z,w, periods two,three and ordinary two-step skew descent. For 6|L, full r5 still follows but full r3 is not proved here. At n4 a nonKoszul nozz object could only have N=9,15,21,...; existence remains unproved. No general assertion of standard Hilbert, Koszulity or noetherianity.

The explicit formal 2x2 Euler matrix with q=(1-t)^2, diagonals q^2+a^2t^2,q^2 and off-diagonals -atq has AS-type degree-four reciprocity, nonnegative Betti signs, det=(1-t)^8 and entrywise nonnegative polynomial-growth inverse. Its generator matrix has Perron root 4+a>4. This is not a realized algebra and fails domain leading-Laurent component comparison, since diagonal pole orders differ. Thus those formal Euler conditions alone do not prove a matrix generator bound.

For any word-Koszul Qn_dom, its finite folded Ext algebra E has the heavy dual zeta normal in the sense E zeta=zeta E. Domain mixed projections yield eta X subset X eta+S zeta^2 S and the reverse inclusion. With eta^2=0, E/(zeta)=Fbar+Fbar eta has excess support only 0 and 2. No nozz, r5 saturation, H, noetherian or period-one assumption. This does not assert a normalizing automorphism for the zero-divisor zeta.

Every word-Koszul Qn_dom, for arbitrary n>=1, has all r3=r4=n,r5=1, a Koszul ASn pure base B, full indexed two-step Ore structure, D3,N=n+2,L=n+5 and standard bigraded row Hilbert series. No additional H/noetherian/nozz/period-one/mixed-rank hypothesis. GS gives r5 not identically zero and D>=3. The AS complement of any pure element annihilating zeta lies in zeta E, proving F->F zeta injective and r3=n. If eta zeta=0, its complement is killed by the quotient support unless D4. At D4, F^(d-2) pairs with E^2_e4=R6*=0, hence vanishes, so the quotient component (d-1,2)=Fbar^(d-2) eta is zero as well; the complement again lies in zeta E and gives a contradiction. Thus all r5=1 and the existing rank criterion applies. No exceptional Koszul dimension remains. Unrestricted non-Koszul objects are not settled.

For every word-Koszul Qn_dom with n even, normal-z period two and odd AS period L=n+5 combine to give actual word-preserving period one and ordinary graded two-step Ore descent over a Koszul ASn domain. No noetherian assumption. Universal odd-n descent is not concluded and is false at n1.

No nonKoszul example satisfying all Qn_dom hypotheses has been constructed, and none was found in the primary sources checked in this update; this is not a complete nonexistence or literature-exhaustion result. At n4, N9,12,... are unexcluded top-word possibilities, not realized families. The classical quadratic Heisenberg U(h2) is a noetherian domain, AS5 with four minimal generators, H=(1-t)^-4(1-t^2)^-1 and minimal shifts 0,1,2,4,5,6 (Floystad-Vatne arXiv0911.5129v3 Theorem2.1/Remark3.2). It is nonKoszul but misses generatorcount=ASdim. Its quadratic dual has H=1+4t+5t^2 while full Ext has higher generators. For any finite-dimensional positively graded Lie g, augmentation indecomposables are g/[g,g], so ASdim-minus-minimalgen equals dim[g,g]; only abelian enveloping algebras satisfy equality. These are known-example and elementary comparison statements, not a new target counterexample.

Conditional on Q4dom with N9: E3 internal words4 and5 annihilate E1 and E2 on both sides yet are paired with each other into E6 word9. Every E3 word>3 survives the quotient by the two-sided ideal generated by zeta, since degree-three elements in that ideal have word3. If either word4/5 middle component is nonzero, the AS pairing of top excess3 forces a surviving odd-excess component in E/(zeta). This is a support consequence, not existence of these components or an N9 exclusion.

For Qn_dom with D3 and a word-preserving period L divisible by three, the heavy-w boundary P(epsilon^2,epsilon^-1) has strictly positive right and left kernels in K=ker(I-S^3) for each fixed 0<epsilon<1, satisfying h_i>=epsilon h_(i+2), g_(i+2)>=epsilon g_i. Rational leading Laurent coefficients of H(epsilon^2/c,c/epsilon) at c1 give normalized rational kernels analytic at epsilon0, even when the boundary kernel has higher dimension. This does not say that K is invariant under P or determine the Hilbert pole order.

For a word-quadratic Z-domain with Tor3(word3,excess4)=0, a relation w_i v=z_i z_(i+2) forces t_i t_(i+2)=0, and x w_(i+1)=z_i z_(i+2) forces t_(i-3)t_(i-1)=0. If b_i=n+1 both constraints hold. Cancellation creates another quadratic relation and a nonzero (R tensor W) intersection (W tensor R) in the forbidden bidegree. D3 ensures the vanishing hypothesis.

For any quadratic Z-domain with primitive jumps (1^n,2,3), t_(i+3k)=0 and t_(i+2+3k)=1 for 0<=k<M, and b_(i+3k)=n+1 for 0<=k<=M, imply M+1<=n. The result also holds after interchanging zero and one in the first two hypotheses. The M+1 one-z words are independent in defect degree one; common z multiplication is injective, and maximal R4 rank compresses the images into w^(M+1)V of dimension at most n. No AS, growth or period hypothesis.

For Qn_dom with D3 and 3|L, at least two full mod-three classes have t_i=r5(i)=1 at every position. If exactly r,r+1 are saturated, b_i=r4(i)=n pointwise on class r+1. If all r5=1, then every b_i<=n and one entire class has b_i=n. Applies unconditionally to every Q4dom for every N, not only N9. Pointwise boundary equations, cubic obstruction, defect propagation and the finite single-z collapse exclude the one-saturated class and the indicated two-saturated deficit. Full r5 and all r3 remain unproved.

For a word-graded positive locally finite Z-algebra with primitive jumps (1^n,2,3), actual word-preserving period L, finite finitely generated simple resolutions and polynomial row growth, m(detP)=0. If all pure w products are nonzero, let g=gcd(L,3): detP_B(u) and (1-(uv^2)^(L/g))^g divide detP(u,v) in Z[u,v]; they are coprime so their product divides. The proof uses integer constant term one and analytic Hilbert inverses, the established Issa-Lalin Theorem1.2(s1), and a proved Jensen equality face lemma. Parity under (x,y)->(-x,-y) gives polynomial rather than Laurent descent. No AS reciprocity, Koszulity or noetherianity is required after the explicit hypotheses. Factor multiplicity does not determine boundary corank.

For a quadratic Z-domain with primitive jumps (1^n,2,3), actual word-preserving period L and polynomial row growth, zero projection of all R4 to zz forces every r5=1. In A/(V) the partial wz->zw scalar relations have no overlaps; one missing position yields two equal-jump normal words whose arbitrary concatenations give exponential growth. No AS, finite global dimension, Koszulity, noetherianity or divisibility restriction on L.

In the D3 two-saturated branch with classes0,1 full and class2 not full, positive analytic exact-K kernels necessarily have leading supports h(0)=e2 and g(0)=e1 after normalization. With h2=g1=1, h0=kappa epsilon+...,h1=nu epsilon^2+...,g0=lambda epsilon+...,g2=mu epsilon^2+..., with nu>=kappa>=1 and mu>=lambda>=1. Any positive leading class0 coordinate forces maximal b on a whole class and violates the forward or reverse finite single-z lemma. No corank-one or Hilbert pole-order conclusion.

For Qn_dom with D3, L=3ell>=9 and all r5=1, put a_i=r3(i),b_i=r4(i),H_i=Tor3(word3,excess3) dimension. Then sum(a_i-H_i)+sum(b_i-n)=0. Exact full-matrix trace calculation yields x^3 coefficient y^(2ell-1)/(1-y^(2ell)) times that sum in detP(x^2,y/x)/(1-y^(2ell))^3; the face-factor theorem forces the coefficient polynomial. No classwise constancy of b_i is assumed. For n4, H_i=p_(i+6,N-3). This is a necessary identity, not automatic Koszulity.

For Q4dom, h_j=p_(j+6,N-3)=dim diagonal E3_excess3 at j, u_j=t_(j+1)a_j, v_j=t_j a_(j+3), h_j<=min(b_j,b_(j+2),u_j+v_j,1+min(u_j,v_j)). Both neighboring t zero imply h=0; one zero implies h<=1. Thus q_i=1,t_(i+N-3)=0 forces a nonzero lower-word pure third syzygy. Also dim diagonal E3_excess2 at j <=min(r_j+a_j,r_(j+3)+a_(j+2)); equality forces injectivity and a direct sum in the displayed normal form. Uses the quadratic-dual diagonal subalgebra, never generation of full Ext in degree one.

open_problems.problem: The arbitrary-n word-Koszul indexed case is fully solved by INDEXED-KOSZUL-ORE without H/noetherian/nozz/period-one assumptions. Remaining scope: For every Qn_dom object with n>=4 and without word-Koszulity, force all r3(i)=n,r5(i)=1 or construct a counterexample. INDEXED-NORMAL-Z-ORE proves these rank conditions equivalent to B-ASn and sufficient for full indexed Ore, without H/Koszul/noetherianity. At n4 this is the tenth condition equivalent to all the Koszul/period/Hilbert/Ore conditions. n1,n2,n3 are solved. At n4 only N=9,12,15,... remain outside the known N6 branch, by unconditional three-divisibility.

Force all r3=n,r5=1 in nonKoszul Qn_dom; the normal-z criterion then supplies PBW/base AS/Ore. At n4, D3 and three-divisibility hold; exactly one saturated class is excluded. Residual two-saturated classes0,1 have b1=4 and positive kernel leading supports e2/e1. Full-r5 residual has all b<=4, one class b4 and sum(a-p_(N-3))+sum(b-4)=0. Start N9/L12 and calculate x4,x5 polynomiality constraints of the Euler determinant divided by its heavy face cube, together with cubic Ext bounds and pure/mixed moments. At general n, nozz gives all r5; D3 gives the two-class theorem; D>3 is still a separate issue. No residual target example is known.

The arbitrary-n word-Koszul indexed case is fully solved by INDEXED-KOSZUL-ORE without H/noetherian/nozz/period-one assumptions. Remaining scope: B-ASn is now equivalent within Qn_dom to r3=n,r5=1. Its derivation, the second normal quotient and non-Koszul PBW are solved under those ranks; remaining work is rank automaticity, or a direct B-AS argument that would imply it. RS non-AS examples cannot be Q4dom pure bases.

At n4 all ten conditions, including A period one, Koszulity, B-AS4 and ordinary two-step Ore descent, are equivalent; their automaticity is open. For n>=5 determine descent conditions. Under B-AS, even L_B gives descent from periods two and L_B+5. n1 has the exact alpha^2=c beta^2 criterion; all n2,n3 domains descend.

Secondary n=2 question; domainness is permitted in the current main problem and need not be proved first. Determine whether every object of Q is a Z-domain by the equivalent condition that the seven jump-2, word-length-one generators z_0,...,z_6 of a chosen word-quadratic presentation have zero left and right annihilators in every degree. All relation counts and Hilbert series are now standard. Begin with kernels of the two projections of R_3 and vanishing coefficients of the one-dimensional R_5, then control possible higher-degree annihilators using AS duality and exact Koszul resolutions. Finite-degree injectivity checks alone do not settle the question.

Under the proved standard relation dimensions, determine whether degenerate mixed projections can occur in Q. Analyze the Vz/zV projections of the two-dimensional R_3 and the Vw/wV/zz projections of the two-dimensional R_4; do not assume the two coefficients of the one-dimensional R_5 are nonzero. Start with a vanishing R_5 coefficient or an R_3 projection of rank below two and derive its cubic syzygies, then check compatibility with the full AS resolution. The relation counts themselves and Q=H=S are already proved. R5-ORIENTATION-OBSTRUCTION excludes opposite one-sided relations at relative distances 2,3,4 modulo 7; focus on remaining distances 1,5,6 and configurations with only one orientation.

Use the proved finite necessary-and-sufficient criterion ORE-FULL-ISOM to obtain normal forms, stabilizers, components and specializations for general quantum- or Jordan-plane Ore data. Separate the L=0 and L!=0 cases, eigenspace coincidences and Jordan forms of J, while retaining the quadratic relation and both L compatibility conditions. The diagonal quantum involution quotient is already complete and is a regression family.

Determine structural branches and necessary/sufficient AS and Koszul conditions inside the fixed standard-rank seven-window parameter space, especially candidates with zero divisors. All actual objects of Q have relation counts (1,2,2,1). The mixed-rank computation excludes other rank arrays under AS hypotheses; it does not certify AS-regularity of arbitrary candidates. Finite Frobenius duality alone is also insufficient.
Construct or exclude objects of Q with least period seven; any such object has zero divisors. Domain Ore families cannot supply such examples.

Classify all standard-rank objects Q=H=S up to indexed isomorphism and determine irreducible components, specializations, stabilizers and relative descent, including any zero-divisor loci. Numerical type exhaustion is complete. The diagonal quantum family has a proved dimension-three finite quotient; do not extrapolate this to the whole Ore or AS parameter space.

For n>=3 and fixed global dimension n+2 and prescribed Hilbert series, determine whether arbitrary weighted-homogeneous relations admit the canonical iterated Ore flag. First analyze n=3 augmentation initial relations without assuming the associated graded algebra remains quadratic or AS-regular.

The arbitrary-n word-Koszul indexed case is fully solved by INDEXED-KOSZUL-ORE without H/noetherian/nozz/period-one assumptions. Remaining scope: At n4 prove automaticity of the ten equivalent conditions, most directly r3=4,r5=1. At n>=5 prove the same two rank conditions for non-Koszul objects; the general normal-z theorem removes any need to prove Koszulity/H/noetherianity first. Ordinary graded word-Koszul objects already have full Ore structure without initial H/noetherianity. Automatic noetherianity for arbitrary-dimensional AS bases is not asserted.
